claim: Female mouse preimplantation embryos undergo an imprinted form of X chromosome inactivation (iXCI) that requires both Rlim (also known as Rnf12) and the long non-coding RNA Xist.
source: Mammalian X-linked gene expression is highly regulated as female cells contain two and male one X chromosome (X). To adjust the X gene dosage between genders, female mouse preimplantation embryos undergo an imprinted form of X chromosome inactivation (iXCI) that requires both Rlim (also known as Rnf12) and the long non-coding RNA Xist.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work and is part of established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Gene expression from the single active X is thought to be upregulated to correct for bi-allelic autosomal (A) gene expression.
source: Moreover, it is thought that gene expression from the single active X is upregulated to correct for bi-allelic autosomal (A) gene expression.
evidence: This claim is presented as a hypothesis or prevailing theory in the field, indicated by 'it is thought that'.

claim: Rlim is crucial for the maintenance of high Xist RNA levels in female embryos at blastocyst stages.
source: Our results reveal crucial roles of Rlim for the maintenance of high Xist RNA levels, Xist clouds and X-silencing in female embryos at blastocyst stages, while initial Xist expression appears Rlim-independent.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript showing differences in Xist levels between WT and Rlim KO embryos.

claim: Initial Xist expression appears Rlim-independent.
source: Our results reveal crucial roles of Rlim for the maintenance of high Xist RNA levels, Xist clouds and X-silencing in female embryos at blastocyst stages, while initial Xist expression appears Rlim-independent.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq and RNA FISH data showing similar Xist expression at early stages in WT and Rlim KO embryos.

claim: X/A upregulation is initiated in early male and female preimplantation embryos.
source: We find further that X/A upregulation is initiated in early male and female preimplantation embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing increasing X/A ratios during preimplantation development.

claim: Female cells inactivate one X in a process known as X chromosome inactivation (XCI) to correct for male/female (F/M) gene dosage imbalances.
source: This is due to the fact that female cells inactivate one X in a process known as X chromosome inactivation (XCI), to correct for male/female (F/M) gene dosage imbalances caused by the presence of two X chromosomes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about X chromosome inactivation.

claim: Male and female cells upregulate gene expression from the single active X two-fold to adjust for X/autosomal (X/A) imbalances.
source: In addition, to adjust for X/autosomal (X/A) imbalances arising from transcription of both autosomal copies of most genes, it is thought that male and female cells upregulate gene expression from the single active X two-fold.
evidence: This claim is presented as a hypothesis based on prior knowledge, indicated by 'it is thought that'.

claim: Imprinted XCI (iXCI) exclusively silences the paternally inherited X (Xp) beginning at the 4-cell stage in female mouse embryos.
source: Beginning at the 4-cell stage in female mouse embryos, imprinted XCI (iXCI) exclusively silences the paternally inherited X (Xp), and this pattern of XCI is maintained in extraembryonic trophoblast cells.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Disteche, 2012; Payer and Lee, 2014; Galupa and Heard, 2015).

claim: Epiblast cells in the inner cell mass (ICM) of blastocysts reactivate the Xp and undergo random form of XCI (rXCI) around implantation (E5-E5.5).
source: In contrast, epiblast cells in the inner cell mass (ICM) of blastocysts that will give rise to the embryo reactivate the Xp and undergo a random form of XCI (rXCI) around implantation (E5-E5.5) (Disteche, 2012; Payer and Lee, 2014; Galupa and Heard, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Disteche, 2012; Payer and Lee, 2014; Galupa and Heard, 2015).

claim: Xist progressively paints the X chromosome from which it is synthesized, triggering repressive histone modifications including H3K27me3.
source: During XCI the long non-coding RNA Xist progressively paints the X chromosome from which it is synthesized, thereby triggering repressive histone modifications including H3K27me3 (Plath et al., 2003) and transcriptional silencing of X-linked genes (Disteche, 2012; Payer and Lee, 2014; Galupa and Heard, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Plath et al., 2003; Disteche, 2012; Payer and Lee, 2014; Galupa and Heard, 2015).

claim: Xist is required both for iXCI and rXCI.
source: Xist is required both for iXCI and rXCI (Marahrens et al., 1997; Penny et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Marahrens et al., 1997; Penny et al., 1996).

claim: Rlim encodes a ubiquitin ligase that shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm.
source: The X-linked gene Rlim encodes a ubiquitin ligase (Ostendorff et al., 2002) that shuttles between the nucleus and cytoplasm (Jiao et al., 2013) and modulates transcription via regulating nuclear multiprotein complexes (Bach et al., 1999; Güngör et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Ostendorff et al., 2002; Jiao et al., 2013; Bach et al., 1999; Güngör et al., 2007).

claim: Rlim promotes the formation of Xist clouds both during iXCI in female mice and in female embryonic stem cells (ESCs) undergoing rXCI in culture.
source: Rlim promotes the formation of Xist clouds both during iXCI in female mice (Shin et al., 2010) and in female embryonic stem cells (ESCs) undergoing rXCI in culture (van Bemmel et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Shin et al., 2010; van Bemmel et al., 2016).

claim: Rlim is dispensable for rXCI in epiblast cells in mice.
source: In mice, however, Rlim is dispensable for rXCI in epiblast cells (Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work (Shin et al., 2014).

claim: Evidence for X/A upregulation was observed in adult mouse tissues, mouse ES cells, and epiblast cells at blastocyst stages.
source: Moreover, while evidence for X/A upregulation was observed not only in adult mouse tissues but also in mouse ES cells and epiblast cells at blastocyst stages (Deng et al., 2013, 2011, 2007), details on the developmental X upregulation are lacking.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Deng et al., 2013, 2011, 2007).

claim: Rlim is required for maintenance of Xist clouds and iXCI in female embryos at blastocyst stages.
source: Analyses of WT, Rlim-knockout (KO) or Xist-KO embryos reveal that Rlim is required for maintenance of Xist clouds and iXCI in female embryos at blastocyst stages.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq and RNA FISH data presented in the manuscript.

claim: X dosage compensation via iXCI in female mice occurs concurrently with a general X/A upregulation in both male and female preimplantation embryos.
source: In addition, our data uncover that X dosage compensation via iXCI in female mice occurs concurrently with a general X/A upregulation in both male and female preimplantation embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing X/A ratios in male and female embryos.

claim: Early embryos consist of a limited number of cell types: essentially one totipotent cell type up to E3, and three cell types at blastocyst stages - epiblast, trophoblast and primitive endoderm cells.
source: This is a valid strategy because (1) early embryos consist of a limited number of cell types: essentially one totipotent cell type up to E3, and three cell types at blastocyst stages - epiblast, trophoblast and primitive endoderm cells - that express known marker genes
evidence: This is established knowledge about mouse embryo development.

claim: Cells of preimplantation embryos undergo iXCI that exclusively silences the Xp.
source: (2) cells of preimplantation embryos undergo iXCI that exclusively silences the Xp
evidence: This is established knowledge about iXCI in mouse embryos.

claim: In mice there is only a relatively small number of genes that escape XCI.
source: (3) in mice there is only a relatively small number of genes that escape XCI (Yang et al., 2010; Finn et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Yang et al., 2010; Finn et al., 2014).

claim: RlimcKOm/Δp-SC females appear healthy, fertile and lack RLIM in all somatic tissues as well as their germline.
source: These females appear healthy, fertile and lack RLIM in all somatic tissues as well as their germline (Figure 1A,B) (Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 1A,B and citation to prior work (Shin et al., 2014).

claim: The gender of each embryo was determined by assessing expression of Y-linked genes, which occurs only in male embryos, and Xist, which is expressed only in females.
source: The gender of each embryo was determined by assessing expression of Y-linked genes, which occurs only in male embryos, and Xist, which is expressed only in females (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: There are no significant differences in gene expression at the chromosome level between RlimΔ/Y and WT/Y males.
source: As expected, comparing Log2-transformed data of 10552 annotated genes that are expressed at all examined developmental stages revealed no significant differences in gene expression at the chromosome level between RlimΔ/Y and WT/Y males (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), consistent with the finding that male mice lacking Rlim develop normally (Shin et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and citation to prior work (Shin et al., 2010).

claim: The developmental transcript profiles of WT embryos matched well with expression of epiblast markers Pou5f1 (Oct4) and Nanog and trophoblast marker Krt8 (Troma1).
source: Analyses of WT embryos (pooled male and female embryos for each stage), showed that the developmental transcript profiles matched well with expression of epiblast markers Pou5f1 (Oct4) (Rosner et al., 1990; Schöler et al., 1990) and Nanog (Chambers et al., 2003; Mitsui et al., 2003) and trophoblast marker Krt8 (Troma1) (Brûlet and Jacob, 1982) (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1F and citations to prior work (Rosner et al., 1990; Schöler et al., 1990; Chambers et al., 2003; Mitsui et al., 2003; Brûlet and Jacob, 1982).

claim: Rlim RNA levels decreased from the 4-cell to the 8-cell stage, possibly due to depletion of maternal pools, then gradually increased up to E3.5, and decreased thereafter.
source: Rlim RNA levels decreased from the 4-cell to the 8-cell stage, possibly due to depletion of maternal pools, then gradually increased up to E3.5, and decreased thereafter (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1F. The explanation about maternal pool depletion is speculative.

claim: High relative levels of Rlim were detected in trophoblasts.
source: High relative levels of Rlim were detected in trophoblasts, suggesting that the cells of the ICM are mostly responsible for the diminished Rlim levels in E4.5 embryos, consistent with a drop in RLIM protein levels specifically in epiblast cells (Shin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and citation to prior work (Shin et al., 2014).

claim: Xist levels in WT female embryos increased dramatically from the 4-cell to the 8-cell stages and peaked around E3.5.
source: Xist levels in WT female embryos increased dramatically from the 4-cell to the 8-cell stages and peaked around E3.5 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The developmental onset of Xist was similar in RlimΔ/Δ females, but significantly lower levels of Xist were measured only after E3.5.
source: Consistent with the detection of Xist transcription foci in early Rlim KO female embryos (Shin et al., 2010), the developmental onset of Xist was similar in RlimΔ/Δ females, but significantly lower levels of Xist were measured only after E3.5 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A and citation to prior work (Shin et al., 2010).

claim: Strand-specific RT-qPCR confirmed that RlimΔ/Δ females expressed similar levels of Xist when compared to WT/WT at E2.5, but much lower levels at E3.5 and thereafter.
source: Moreover, strand-specific RT-qPCR confirmed that RlimΔ/Δ females expressed similar levels of Xist when compared to WT/WT at E2.5, but much lower levels at E3.5 and thereafter (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Xist clouds were detected in WT embryos at E2.5 morula and E3.5 blastocyst stages.
source: As expected, Xist clouds were detected in WT embryos of both embryonic stages (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 2B–D.

claim: In Xist cloud-positive RlimΔ/Δ embryos at E2.5, the number of cells displaying clouds was highly variable, ranging between 1 cell to most cells.
source: In contrast to WT/WT, however, in Xist cloud-positive RlimΔ/Δ embryos at E2.5, the number of cells displaying clouds was highly variable, ranging between 1 cell to most cells (Figure 2B,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 2B,D.

claim: At E3.5 the vast majority of cells exhibited transcription foci for Xist and only few cells displayed Xist clouds in RlimΔ/Δ embryos.
source: As expected, at E3.5 the vast majority of cells exhibited transcription foci for Xist and only few cells displayed Xist clouds in RlimΔ/Δ embryos (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Rlim is dispensable for initial Xist expression in 4-cell stage embryos but required for upregulation/maintenance of Xist expression after E3.
source: Combined, these data reveal that Rlim is dispensable for initial Xist expression in 4-cell stage embryos but required for upregulation/maintenance of Xist expression after E3.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RNA-seq and RNA FISH data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Xist clouds transiently form in RlimΔ/Δ female morulae, which cannot be maintained at blastocyst stages.
source: They further show that Xist clouds transiently form in RlimΔ/Δ female morulae, which cannot be maintained at blastocyst stages.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH data showing Xist clouds at E2.5 but not E3.5 in Rlim KO embryos.

claim: In female WT/WT embryos the X gene dosage was close to two-fold that of males at early developmental stages and then, starting at morula stages, gradually decreased to a gene dosage similar to that of males by late blastocyst stages.
source: In female WT/WT embryos the gene dosage was close to two-fold that of males at early developmental stages (likely due to two active X chromosomes) and then, starting at morula stages, gradually decreased to a gene dosage similar to that of males by late blastocyst stages, consistent with Xp silencing (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The X gene dosage in female RlimΔ/Δ embryos was not significantly different from that of WT/WT females up to E3, revealing a partial silencing of X-linked genes at these early stages in the absence of RLIM.
source: Consistent with the formation of transient Xist clouds (Figure 2) the X gene dosage in female RlimΔ/Δ embryos was not significantly different from that of WT/WT females up to E3, revealing a partial silencing of X-linked genes at these early stages in the absence of RLIM.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The continued further silencing of X-linked genes observed in WT/WT during blastocyst stages was significantly inhibited in RlimΔ/Δ females.
source: However, the continued further silencing of X-linked genes observed in WT/WT during blastocyst stages was significantly inhibited in RlimΔ/Δ females (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The detection of initial X-silencing at late morula/early blastocyst stages via RNA-seq on whole embryos fits well with published data obtained by RNA FISH that show diminished transcription foci of X-linked protein-encoding genes generally starting between the 8-cell and morula stages.
source: Considering an estimated average half-life of around 10 hr for mRNAs in mammalian cells (Yang et al., 2003) including mouse preimplantation embryos (Kidder and Pedersen, 1982), the detection of initial X-silencing at late morula/early blastocyst stages via RNA-seq on whole embryos (Figure 3A) fits well with published data obtained by RNA FISH that show diminished transcription foci of X-linked protein-encoding genes generally starting between the 8-cell and morula stages (Patrat et al., 2009; Namekawa et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A and citations to prior work (Yang et al., 2003; Kidder and Pedersen, 1982; Patrat et al., 2009; Namekawa et al., 2010).

claim: Gene silencing during iXCI occurs within most regions on the X chromosome.
source: Indeed, examination of the silencing pattern of 351 annotated X-linked genes in WT females showed that gene silencing occurs within most regions on the X chromosome both during the early (8-cell to E3) and late phase (E3 to E4.5) of iXCI (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The KO of Rlim or Xist affects global expression levels of X-linked transcripts but not those expressed from autosomes.
source: Our analyses of global gene expression profiles in females shows that the KO of Rlim or Xist affects global expression levels of X-linked transcripts but not those expressed from autosomes (Figures 3B; 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figures 3B and 5B.

claim: In B6m/CASTp embryos at E3.5, only around 50% of X-linked CAST transcripts were measured when compared to transcripts originating from the B6 X chromosome.
source: Indeed, in B6m/CASTp embryos we measured only around 50% of X-linked CAST transcripts when compared to transcripts originating from the B6 X chromosome (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by allele-specific RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C.

claim: An R26C-mediated deletion of the Rlim allele on the Xm led to embryonic lethality in a female-specific parent-of-origin effect.
source: Indeed, an R26C-mediated deletion of the Rlim allele on the Xm led to embryonic lethality in a female-specific parent-of-origin effect (Figure 4A,B), similar to the germline Rlim KO (Shin et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic data shown in Figure 4A,B and citation to prior work (Shin et al., 2010).

claim: A maternally transmitted floxed Rlim allele was no longer detectable at E3.5 in R26C-mediated cKO embryos.
source: This deletion proved highly penetrant, as a maternally transmitted floxed Rlim allele was no longer detectable at early stages of the second iXCI phase (E3.5; Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Xist cloud formation was strongly diminished in trophoblasts of female R26C-mediated cKOm blastocysts isolated at E4 and cultured ex vivo for 2 days.
source: RNA FISH experiments showed that Xist cloud formation was strongly diminished in trophoblasts of female R26C-mediated cKOm blastocysts isolated at E4 and cultured ex vivo for 2 days (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Embryonic RLIM expressed from the maternal allele plays crucial roles for the maintenance of Xist clouds during iXCI.
source: These data provide genetic confirmation that embryonic RLIM expressed from the maternal allele plays crucial roles for the maintenance of Xist clouds during iXCI.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the genetic and RNA FISH data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Only male but no female pups were born from XistcKO/Y-SC males mated with WT/WT females.
source: XistcKO/Y males were mated with WT/WT females (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) and, confirming the previously observed sex-specific parent-of-origin embryonic lethality (Marahrens et al., 1997), only male but no female pups were born (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and citation to prior work (Marahrens et al., 1997).

claim: The F/M expression profiles of X-linked genes were high in XistWT/Δp embryos of all stages.
source: Confirming a central role for the Xist lncRNA during iXCI, the F/M expression profiles of X-linked genes were high in XistWT/Δp embryos of all stages (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: XistWT/Δp females show significant defects in X dosage compensation at around E3.5 blastocyst stages when compared with WT/WT.
source: Comparisons with WT/WT revealed significant defects in X dosage compensation in XistWT/Δp females at around E3.5 blastocyst stages (Figure 5D), consistent with published findings (Namekawa et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 5D and citation to prior work (Namekawa et al., 2010).

claim: The average F/M ratios of females of all genotypes (WT/WT, RlimΔ/Δ and XistWT/Δp) remained below 2 even at early developmental stages, likely explained by a previously reported Xist-independent partial silencing of some X-linked transcripts.
source: The finding that the average F/M ratios of females of all genotypes (WT/WT, RlimΔ/Δ and XistWT/Δp) remained below 2 even at early developmental stages (Figures 2A; 5C) is likely explained by a previously reported Xist-independent partial silencing of some X-linked transcripts (Kalantry et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figures 2A and 5C and citation to prior work (Kalantry et al., 2009).

claim: The general pre/peri-implantation profile of X dosage compensation between genders as observed in WT female mice is remarkably similar to that measured in early female human embryos.
source: Our results reveal that the general pre/peri-implantation profile of X dosage compensation between genders as observed in WT female mice (Figure 3A) is remarkably similar to that measured in early female human embryos (Petropoulos et al., 2016), even though mice but not humans undergo iXCI (Okamoto et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A and citations to prior work (Petropoulos et al., 2016; Okamoto et al., 2011).

claim: Unlike in mice, there is no sign of X upregulation in human preimplantation embryos.
source: It is thus surprising that unlike in mice (Figure 6) there is no sign of X upregulation in human preimplantation embryos (Petropoulos et al., 2016) (not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Petropoulos et al., 2016) and comparison with data in Figure 6.

claim: X-linked gene expression is upregulated at post-implantation stages in humans.
source: Because X/A values in adult human somatic tissues are close to 1 (Deng et al., 2011), this suggests that X-linked gene expression is upregulated at post-implantation stages.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that X/A values are close to 1 in adult tissues but not in preimplantation embryos, combined with citation to prior work (Deng et al., 2011).

claim: Crucial roles for both Rlim and Xist are restricted to X dosage compensation in females.
source: Our analyses of global gene expression profiles in females shows that the KO of Rlim or Xist affects global expression levels of X-linked transcripts but not those expressed from autosomes (Figures 3B; 5B). This combined with the fact that males lacking either Xist or Rlim appear healthy and are fertile indicates that crucial roles for both genes are restricted to X dosage compensation in females.
evidence: This claim is inferred from RNA-seq data shown in Figures 3B and 5B and the observation that males lacking these genes are healthy.

claim: High levels of Xist, the maintenance of Xist clouds and X-dosage compensation in female blastocysts depend on Rlim.
source: Indeed, our results reveal that high levels of Xist, the maintenance of Xist clouds and X-dosage compensation in female blastocysts depend on Rlim.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq and RNA FISH data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: RLIM's function on iXCI is exerted through regulation of Xist.
source: Combined, these results imply that RLIM's function on iXCI is exerted through regulation of Xist.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that Rlim affects Xist levels and Xist clouds, which in turn affect X-silencing.

claim: Initiation of the iXCI process might occur normally at early stages in RlimKO females.
source: Moreover, because only iXCI globally and significantly influences X-linked gene expression specifically in females, the development of temporary Xist clouds in RlimKO females (Figure 2) and a similar silencing pattern at E3 between WT/WT and RlimKO females (Figure 3; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C) suggests that initiation of the iXCI process might occur normally at early stages in RlimKO females.
evidence: This claim is inferred from RNA-seq and RNA FISH data shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: At blastocyst stages X-silencing and iXCI cannot be maintained in RlimKO females, leading to a failure in X dosage compensation.
source: However, at blastocyst stages X-silencing and iXCI cannot be maintained leading to a failure in X dosage compensation (Figure 3; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: RLIM protein levels are down-regulated specifically in epiblast cells of E4.5 blastocyst embryos.
source: In this context, it is important to note that RLIM protein levels are down-regulated specifically in epiblast cells of E4.5 blastocyst embryos (Shin et al., 2014), at a time point when these cells start to reactivate the Xp (Mak et al., 2004; Okamoto et al., 2004) before undergoing rXCI.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Shin et al., 2014; Mak et al., 2004; Okamoto et al., 2004).

claim: RLIM down-regulation provides an attractive molecular mechanism for triggering the Xp reactivation process.
source: Thus, because RLIM is crucial for the maintenance of iXCI at peri-implantation stages (Figures 2–4), this down-regulation provides an attractive molecular mechanism for triggering the Xp reactivation process.
evidence: This claim is speculative, inferred from the data and prior knowledge about RLIM function and Xp reactivation.

claim: Upregulation of X-linked transcripts is initiated in early male and female mouse embryos.
source: In summary, by elucidating the mouse pre- and peri-implantation transcriptome, this study provides a comprehensive view on X linked gene expression during early mouse development. Our analyses uncover that upregulation of X-linked transcripts is initiated in early male and female mouse embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing increasing X/A ratios during preimplantation development.

claim: In females X upregulation occurs concomitant with iXCI, which progressively leads to X gene dosage compensation between genders in an Rlim and Xist-dependent manner.
source: In females X upregulation occurs concomitant with iXCI, which progressively leads to X gene dosage compensation between genders in an Rlim and Xist-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing X/A ratios and F/M ratios in WT and mutant embryos.

claim: Mapping reads from WT and KO embryos to the Rlim locus showed that the deleted region in KO embryos was not represented.
source: Mapping reads from WT and KO embryos to the Rlim locus showed that the deleted region in KO embryos was not represented (Figure 1E; data not shown), validating both the mating strategy and the specificity of the data obtained via whole embryo RNA-seq.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The general cell type specification events that occur at blastocyst stages were similar in embryos of both WT/WT and RlimΔ/Δ genotypes.
source: The observed variations between replicates were well within margins previously observed for single cell RNA-seq technology (Jaitin et al., 2014; Shalek et al., 2013), and comparison of expression levels of these cell markers between RlimΔ/Δ and WT/WT females suggested that the general cell type specification events that occur at blastocyst stages were similar in embryos of both genotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and citations to prior work (Jaitin et al., 2014; Shalek et al., 2013).

claim: More than 90% of reads in the Tsix/Xist locus map within the Xist transcription unit.
source: We detected a high read density located precisely within the Xist transcription unit (>90% of reads) and very few reads in introns or exons specific to Tsix (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), indicating that the detected reads mostly correspond to Xist RNA.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: RlimΔ/Δ females develop Xist clouds at morula stages, but likely with a slower kinetics when compared to WT/WT females.
source: As few cells of 8-cell staged female embryos lacking RLIM display Xist clouds (Shin et al., 2010), these results indicate that RlimΔ/Δ females develop Xist clouds at morula stages, but likely with a slower kinetics when compared to WT/WT females.
evidence: This claim is inferred from RNA FISH data and citation to prior work (Shin et al., 2010).

claim: The gradual X-silencing from the 8-cell stage to E4.5 in WT/WT females as determined by whole embryo RNA-seq is consistent with the existence of long-lived mRNAs in mouse preimplantation embryos.
source: Moreover, the gradual X-silencing from the 8-cell stage to E4.5 in WT/WT females as determined by whole embryo RNA-seq (Figure 3A) is consistent with the existence of long-lived mRNAs in mouse preimplantation embryos (Kidder and Pedersen, 1982).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3A and citation to prior work (Kidder and Pedersen, 1982).

claim: Silencing of X-linked genes in females occurs across the entire X chromosome.
source: In agreement with published results (Deng et al., 2014; Marks et al., 2015), we show that silencing of X-linked genes in females occurs across the entire X chromosome (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3C and citations to prior work (Deng et al., 2014; Marks et al., 2015).

claim: Xist does not spread linearly along the X chromosome, but rather spreads to multiple loci on the X simultaneously, due to the three dimensional folding of the chromosome.
source: Such spatial concordance of silencing is consistent with studies in ESCs which show that Xist does not spread linearly along the X chromosome, but rather spreads to multiple loci on the X simultaneously, due to the three dimensional folding of the chromosome (Engreitz et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Engreitz et al., 2013).

claim: There is a Xist-independent partial silencing of some X-linked transcripts.
source: The finding that the average F/M ratios of females of all genotypes (WT/WT, RlimΔ/Δ and XistWT/Δp) remained below 2 even at early developmental stages (Figures 2A; 5C) is likely explained by a previously reported Xist-independent partial silencing of some X-linked transcripts (Kalantry et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Kalantry et al., 2009).

claim: Male mouse ES cells and epiblast cells in blastocysts display X/A values of around 0.8.
source: Indeed, male mouse ES cells and epiblast cells in blastocysts display X/A values of around 0.8 (Deng et al., 2013, 2011, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Deng et al., 2013, 2011, 2007).

claim: The total increase in X/A ratio between the 4-cell stage to E4.5 in males was 1.58 fold.
source: Our results revealed gradually increasing levels of transcription from the X relative to autosomes (Figure 6A) and the total increase between the 4-cell stage to E4.5 was 1.58 fold (P<10–11; Students t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6A with statistical analysis.

claim: Among all chromosomes, gene expression from the X displayed the highest increase during preimplantation development in males.
source: When we examined average expression from single chromosomes (normalized against 4-cell stage levels) we observed that, among all chromosomes, gene expression from the X displayed the highest increase (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: At the 4-cell stage, the contribution of the X chromosome to total gene expression in males was around 0.5 fold of the average autosome.
source: These analyses showed that, consistent with the presence of one X chromosome, at the earliest time point measured, the contribution of the X was much lower than that of any autosome, only around 0.5 fold of the average autosome (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The contribution of the X chromosome to total gene expression in males gradually increased to around 0.77 fold measured at E4.5.
source: This contribution gradually increased to around 0.77 fold measured at E4.5, which was the 14th most highly expressed of the 20 chromosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: X upregulation is initiated during preimplantation development.
source: These results are in general agreement with X/A levels previously measured in male murine ES cells as well as epiblast cells (Lin et al., 2007), and indicate that X upregulation is initiated during preimplantation development.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and citation to prior work (Lin et al., 2007).

claim: X/A upregulation is initiated both during male and female preimplantation development.
source: Including female embryos in these analyses (Figure 6D), our data reveal that X/A upregulation is initiated both during male and female preimplantation development, as female RlimΔ/Δ and XistWT/Δp embryos, which are defective in iXCI, display high E4.5/4-cell ratios of 1.58 and 1.75, respectively, similar to those of males (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6D and 6E.

claim: All females start out with high X/A ratios compared to those measured in males (between 1.58–1.87 at the 4-cell stage).
source: Upon examination of early developmental stages, we found that all females start out with high X/A ratios compared to those measured in males (between 1.58–1.87 at the 4-cell stage; Figure 6F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: By E4.5, X/A ratios of RlimΔ/Δ and XistWT/Δp females are still high compared to males (around 1.8 fold), while those of WT/WT females have decreased to levels close to 1.
source: However, by E4.5, whereas X/A ratios of RlimΔ/Δ and XistWT/Δp females are still high compared to males (around 1.8 fold), those of WT/WT females have decreased to levels close to 1 (Figure 6F).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: X upregulation takes place concurrently with iXCI in WT/WT females that compensates the general X gene dosage to that of males.
source: Combined, these results indicate that X upregulation occurs during preimplantation development in males and females. In WT/WT females, X upregulation takes place concurrently with iXCI that compensates the general X gene dosage to that of males.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RNA-seq data showing X/A ratios and F/M ratios.

claim: RLIM protein is rapidly turned-over during early development.
source: Because RLIM protein is rapidly turned-over during early development (Becker et al., 2003; Ostendorff et al., 2002), if RLIM is required for X-silencing only after E3, this predicts that maternal stores of RLIM will not be sufficient for iXCI but that RLIM synthesized by the embryo is required for later stages of the iXCI process.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Becker et al., 2003; Ostendorff et al., 2002).

claim: Embryonic RLIM plays a crucial role for iXCI after E3.
source: To confirm that embryonic RLIM plays a crucial role for iXCI after E3 we targeted the maternally transmitted conditional Rlim allele via a paternally transmitted Rosa26-Cre (R26C) transgene (Soriano, 1999), from which Cre is induced after zygotic genome activation (ZGA).
evidence: This claim is supported by genetic experiments and citation to prior work (Soriano, 1999).

claim: The detection of transcription foci of Xist adjacent to Rlim in R26C-mediated cKOm trophoblasts indicated defects in Xp silencing.
source: Moreover, the detection of transcription foci of Xist adjacent to Rlim in these trophoblasts indicated defects in Xp silencing (Figure 4E), consistent with previously published results (Shin et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA FISH data shown in Figure 4E and citation to prior work (Shin et al., 2010).

claim: XistWT/Δp females are devoid of functional Xist RNA because during iXCI, the Xp is exclusively silenced and Xist is not expressed from the Xm.
source: To functionally connect Rlim and Xist during iXCI we next examined female embryos that carry a germline Xist mutation on the paternally inherited X (XistWT/Δp). These females are devoid of functional Xist RNA because during iXCI, the Xp is exclusively silenced and Xist is not expressed from the Xm.
evidence: This is inferred from the knowledge that iXCI silences the Xp and Xist is only expressed from the inactive X.

claim: The decline in F/M values of X-linked transcripts in females is due to Xp-silencing.
source: These results provide independent confirmation that the decline in F/M values of X-linked transcripts in females (Figure 3A) is due to Xp-silencing.
evidence: This claim is supported by allele-specific RNA-seq data confirming Xp silencing.

claim: There is an early Rlim-independent phase of iXCI in totipotent cells up to around E3 that leads to partial Xp-silencing.
source: Thus, our combined results distinguish an early Rlim-independent phase of iXCI in totipotent cells up to around E3 that leads to partial Xp-silencing, and a late phase after E3 that is Rlim-dependent and leads to robust Xp-silencing.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RNA-seq and RNA FISH data showing similar X-silencing in WT and Rlim KO embryos at early stages.

claim: There is a late phase of iXCI after E3 that is Rlim-dependent and leads to robust Xp-silencing.
source: Thus, our combined results distinguish an early Rlim-independent phase of iXCI in totipotent cells up to around E3 that leads to partial Xp-silencing, and a late phase after E3 that is Rlim-dependent and leads to robust Xp-silencing.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RNA-seq and RNA FISH data showing differences in X-silencing between WT and Rlim KO embryos at late stages.

claim: The process of iXCI progressively adjusts the X-linked gene dosage from the 8-cell stage to E4.5 during early female development.
source: These data further confirm that the process of iXCI progressively adjusts the X-linked gene dosage from the 8-cell stage to E4.5 during early female development.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing gradual decrease in F/M ratios.
